prompt: Draw a quiet landscape with one broad, pale-green hill rising gently across the lower third of the 1920×1200 canvas and a single warm-yellow sun above it. Keep the sky a clean light blue and leave the scene uncluttered.

On a plain cream background, draw one large flower centered on the canvas: a round orange center surrounded by exactly six evenly spaced, rounded pink petals. Make every petal clearly distinct from its neighbors.

Draw a simple 4-by-3 grid of twelve equal square tiles centered on the canvas. Use thin dark outlines, consistent gaps between tiles, and alternate pale blue and pale yellow fills like a checkerboard.

Draw one small cottage on a plain background, with a rectangular blue body and a red triangular roof. The roof should sit directly on the body, extend slightly beyond both side walls, and have a centered rectangular door.

On a dark navy background, draw two concentric rings centered on the canvas: a thick gold outer ring and a thinner mint-green inner ring. Keep the navy center visible and place the gold ring visually behind the mint ring wherever their strokes meet.

Create a crisp, geometric tidal-marsh landscape under a pale peach sky. Layer two angular blue-gray mesas along the horizon, a broad ochre marsh bank in the foreground, and a winding teal channel that narrows as it recedes; add three small rounded clouds well above the mesas.

Draw four distinct flowers in evenly spaced terracotta pots across the canvas, each with exactly seven rounded petals around one circular center. Give each flower a straight green stem and two leaves, and vary the petal colors while keeping the pots and flowers clearly separated.

Make a centered board with exactly six columns and four rows of equal square cells, using thin, even grid lines and generous margins. Place a small filled circle in row 1, column 2; a diamond in row 2, column 5; and a small outlined triangle in row 4, column 3, leaving every other cell empty.

Illustrate three compact houses stepping up a grassy slope from left to right. For each house, make the triangular roof base meet the top of the walls, extend both eaves slightly beyond the wall edges, and keep the door and two windows fully inside the wall shape; let the houses decrease in size as they recede.

Show three thick, cleanly outlined circular hoops in a horizontal chain against a plain light background, with each neighboring pair overlapping. Make the left hoop pass over the middle hoop at their crossing and the middle hoop pass over the right hoop, using interrupted outlines at each crossing so the over-under weave is unmistakable.

Create a stylized dusk landscape on the 1920×1200 canvas using crisp filled shapes and visible, restrained outlines. Build a layered mountain horizon from four angular peaks, with the two tallest peaks framing a narrow pale sun; place a winding river that starts between the central peaks, widens toward the foreground, and ends at the bottom edge. Add a dark foreground ridge with three distinct pine silhouettes and a small cluster of rounded shrubs, keeping the river unobstructed and the sky mostly open.

Draw a botanical arrangement of exactly seven flowers, grouped as three blooms on the left and four on the right, with a clear gap between the groups. Give every flower exactly eight separate rounded petals around one circular center, and connect each bloom to a visible stem that joins a single curved ground line. Add exactly two leaves to each stem, alternating their sides, and vary the bloom sizes while keeping every petal and center clearly countable.

Make a clean geometric poster on a 1920×1200 canvas with a grid spanning from (160,150) to (1760,1050), divided into eight equal columns and five equal rows with thin, faint lines. Center one colored disk in each of these cells, using row-column numbering from the top left: (1,1), (1,8), (2,4), (3,2), (3,7), (4,5), (5,1), (5,4), and (5,8); make all disks the same size and keep them inside their cells. Add three narrow horizontal bars centered in cells (2,2), (3,5), and (4,8), each spanning half a cell width, and use a restrained palette so the grid remains legible.

Illustrate three simple houses on one gently sloping hill, with the middle house largest, the left house half its width, and the right house three-quarters its width. Give every house a triangular roof whose eaves extend equally beyond both walls, one centered door that reaches the ground line, and two equal square windows placed symmetrically on either side of the door. Make each smaller house’s door and windows scale in the same proportion as its walls, and keep all three houses fully separate with visible ground between them.

Create three thick, smooth oval bands interlinked in a horizontal chain on the 1920×1200 canvas, with equal-sized loops centered on the same horizontal line and evenly spaced. At both crossings between each neighboring pair, make the upper crossing show the left-hand loop passing in front and the lower crossing show it passing behind, using clean under-gaps so the weave is unmistakable. Give the three bands distinct coordinated colors, consistent width, and a plain background that leaves generous space around the chain.

Create a crisp, geometric landscape with a pale dawn sky, layered mountain ridges, foothills, and a winding river. Show exactly three prominent triangular mountain peaks, with the center peak tallest and the two outer peaks lower; place a circular sun in the upper-right sky, clear of every peak. A single blue river should emerge from the gap between the foreground foothills and widen continuously toward the bottom edge without branching. Use distinct flat colors and clean filled shapes so the mountain layers and river remain easy to distinguish.

Illustrate a tidy flower garden with exactly three large blossoms in an upper row and exactly six smaller blossoms arranged in two staggered rows below them. Give each large blossom exactly 12 clearly separated oval petals and each small blossom exactly 8, arranged evenly around a visible center. Connect every blossom to its own slender stem, with a few leaves along each stem, and keep the flower heads distinct rather than overlapping. Use a coordinated, cheerful palette and a simple ground strip to anchor the stems.

Draw a precise board grid whose outer rectangle runs from (300, 215) to (1620, 985), divided into 12 columns and 7 rows of equal 110-by-110 cells; make the lines fine but clearly visible. Number columns mentally from left to right and rows from top to bottom, and place one centered blue circle in each of these cells: (2,2), (11,2), (4,3), (9,3), (1,4), (12,4), (4,5), (9,5), (2,6), and (11,6). Place centered gold squares instead in cells (6,2), (7,2), (6,6), and (7,6), leaving every other cell empty; keep all markers comfortably inside their cells.

Draw exactly three detached cottages standing on the same level ground: a large central cottage with a 480-pixel-wide, 330-pixel-high rectangular wall, flanked by two matching cottages whose walls are each 300 pixels wide and 210 pixels high. Give every cottage a centered triangular roof with equal overhang on both sides, and place exactly two equal square windows symmetrically on either side of a centered door; the three doors should have the same width-to-wall-height ratio. Keep the central cottage visibly taller and wider than either neighbor, add a narrow path from its door toward the bottom edge, and keep the path clear of the side cottages.

Create a woven chain of exactly five equal circular rings, each with a thick colored band and a clearly open center, aligned horizontally around the canvas midpoint. Set neighboring ring centers 0.72 ring diameters apart so each adjacent pair crosses twice, while non-neighboring rings remain separate. At the upper crossing of each neighboring pair, make the left ring pass over the right; at its lower crossing, make the right ring pass over the left, using local occlusion so the weave is visible at both crossings. Alternate the band colors along the chain and keep the ring outlines smooth and uninterrupted everywhere except where a band is visibly concealed beneath another.
